growth_thesis.claim: Continued payments volume growth requires that the shift toward digital commerce and electronic payments persists and that consumer spending levels and macroeconomic conditions remain supportive.

growth_thesis.claim: Data processing revenue grew 17% in 2026 to 23,374 (table in millions), driven primarily by a 9% increase in Visa processed transactions to 281,331 (table in millions), select pricing modifications, value-added services growth, and higher cross-border mix.

growth_thesis.claim: International transaction revenue increased 8% in 2026 to 15,251 (table in millions), driven primarily by 15% nominal cross-border volume growth excluding intra-Europe transactions, supported by cross-border ecommerce and travel-related activity.

growth_thesis.claim: Value-added services revenue grew 31% in 2026 to $14.2 billion, led by Issuing Solutions and Advisory and Other Services, pushing other revenue up 40% to 5,677 (table in millions).

growth_thesis.claim: For value-added services growth to continue, industry participants must not withhold transaction data to favor competing offerings, and Visa must adapt its data and AI governance to fragmented privacy, cybersecurity, and AI laws.

Failure to adapt our data governance practices to keep pace with evolving AI technologies, data processing practices, cybersecurity threats, and regulatory requirements could harm our ability to compete, decrease the value of our products and services to clients, and adversely affect our future growth.

growth_thesis.claim: Visa is pursuing an estimated more than $20 trillion annual consumer spend opportunity across cash, check, legacy ACH, A2A, and RTP, while expanding Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, tokenization, Tap to Everything, stablecoin programs, and agentic commerce.
quotes: Of this spend opportunity, we are pursuing an estimated more than $20 trillion annual opportunity in consumer spend, spread across cash, check, legacy Automated Clearing House (ACH), A2A payments, real-time payments (RTP) or other less effective forms of digital payments.
We believe agentic commerce will expand our addressable market and drive future growth.

growth_thesis.claim: To sustain growth, Visa must prevent disintermediation by closed-loop networks, national RTP systems, digital wallets, and stablecoin payment platforms, and preserve network participation as AI and agentic interfaces reshape payment initiation.
quotes: We and our competitors are developing or participating in alternative payment systems, including mobile payments, P2P services, RTP initiatives, ACH/direct debit solutions and cryptocurrency-based platforms, including stablecoin payments, that could reduce our role or disintermediate us from transaction processing.

As AI-enabled commerce continues to evolve, digital wallets, software platforms, agentic commerce experiences, mobile applications and other technologies may increasingly influence payment initiation, credential selection and seller choice.

growth_thesis.claim: For revenue growth to continue, Visa must retain large financial institution clients without margin-eroding pricing or client incentive concessions, and navigate interchange caps, routing mandates, and domestic localization barriers.

National laws protecting domestic providers or mandating local processing continue to evolve in the face of geopolitical developments, may increase costs; affect our ability to effectively compete with local providers, reduce payments volume and net revenue; limit our ability to leverage global processing capabilities; restrict growth, innovation, and market entry; and create new competitors, all of which could materially harm our business and financial results.
